# dsh-session-journal
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web plugin that keeps a **work journal** for each session in the right side
bar. Long sessions scroll away: requirements were discussed, code was written, reviewed three times,
fixed and tested, and by then the start is far out of view. The journal shows what the session has
worked on, where each piece of work stands, and lets you jump back to any turn in the chat.
中文文档
## What you get
- **Now**: whether the session is running, the current phase (for example `Review #2`), a one-line s
tatus, and a highlighted "Your turn" box when the agent stopped to wait for you. Totals for the sess

ion: open items, decisions, turns, time, changed files and lines, tests passed.
- **Work items**: th
e session's turns grouped by purpose (one card per thing it worked on), not by time. Each card shows
its status, the turns it covers, files and tests, and counts of what is still **open** and what was
**decided**, so a card marked done with loose ends says so. Expanded, it shows the goal, the result

, the open items, the decisions, and two lists:
- **Jump to a turn**: one row per turn with what you
asked and the phases it went through. Click a row to scroll the chat to the start of that turn (ear

lier history is loaded first when needed).
- **Changed files**: file name, directory, lines added an

d removed, the phases that touched it. Click to open the file in the sidebar preview.
- **Header chi

p**: the current work item and phase next to the session title; click it to open the journal.
- Engl
ish and Chinese UI, following the DSH language setting. The summary language is a separate choice in
the panel footer: same as the UI, Chinese, or English.
## Usage
Open a session and pick **Work log** on the right sidebar's start page, or click the chip next to th
e session title. Expand a work item to see its open items and decisions; open **Jump to a turn** and
click a row to scroll the chat to that turn. Change the summary language in the panel footer.
## How it works
Facts come from the session log; a model only labels and summarizes.
1. **Facts** (`lib/collector.js`): the plugin reads the session's append-only event log through DSH'
s `sessionQuery` service, so compacted history is still there. Per turn it extracts the user's messa
ge, every tool call, file edits with line counts, test commands and their exit codes, review delegat

ions, questions to the user, and the todo list.
2. **Per-turn summaries** (`lib/summarizer.js`): eac
h finished turn is summarized once by a model into phases (from a fixed list: requirements, research
, design, build, review, fix, test, debug, ship, discussion), a short title and result per phase, th
e decisions made, and what was left open. Text the user pasted from elsewhere (another session's pan

el, logs, someone else's message) is treated as material, not as a request.
3. **Work items** (`lib/
outline.js`): once every finished turn has a summary, one more call groups the turns into 1 to 6 wor
k items and writes each item's status, result, open items and decisions. It sees the whole session,
so problems solved in later turns do not linger as open. It is redone when the summaries change, whi

ch is about one call per new turn.
4. **When it updates** (`lib/autoupdate.js`): as soon as a sessio
n's turn ends, that session's journal is updated in the background: the finished turn is summarized,
then the work items are regrouped. The plugin keeps checking that session every few seconds, as an
open panel would, until nothing is left to do, so a failed summary is tried again after a minute (th
ree attempts in all) without anyone opening the panel. It gives up after five minutes without progre
ss, or thirty in total. Only the session whose turn ended is touched, in one summary language: the o
ne it was last viewed in, else the language of its existing cache, else the language last viewed in
the panel (remembered across restarts). Subagent and teammate sessions are skipped; their parent ses

sion records the delegation.
[该节后续省略]
## Model and cost
By default each session is summarized with **that session's own provider and model**. Summary calls
are separate requests with their own small context; they never touch the conversation or its cache.
Costs, roughly: one call per finished turn (a few thousand input tokens), and one outline call per n
ew turn (5k to 20k input tokens on long sessions). In the background, only sessions that are being w
orked on cost anything; idle sessions are not touched (opening the panel on one still summarizes any
turns it lacks). The first turn to end after installing or upgrading the plugin also summarizes tha
t session's earlier turns that have no summary yet, and so does the first turn of a forked session,
for the turns it inherited.
To use one fixed, usually cheaper, model for every session, set both `SESSION_JOURNAL_PROVIDER` and
`SESSION_JOURNAL_MODEL` in DSH's launch environment (for example `$DSH_HOME/.env`); setting only one
of them has no effect:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH after changing them.
## Jumping to a turn
DSH has no public "scroll to turn" API for plugins. The chat view has its own turn rail, a row of ti
cks at the right edge of the transcript, one per turn. The journal finds the tick for the turn and c
licks it, so the chat does the scrolling and any history loading itself.
- This relies on the chat view's markup, not on a contract. If a DSH update changes the rail, clicki

ng a turn shows a note instead of jumping; nothing else breaks.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
DSH `>=0.2.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` (0.2.x, including its prereleases), Node `>=22.19`.

## Known limitations
- Grouping into work items is done by a model and is not always how you would split the work; for ex

ample a release step may come out as its own item.
- While a turn is running, a work item's open ite

ms can lag one turn behind; they catch up when the turn ends and is summarized.
- Files outside the

session's workspace are listed but cannot be previewed in the sidebar.
- The first time you open a l
ong session that has no cache yet, summarizing every turn takes a minute or two. Until then the pane
l shows rule-based phases.
